points: Counselors handle everyday problems, growth and relationships — strength-based.
Clinical psychologists diagnose and treat mental disorders.
Psychiatrists are medical doctors who can prescribe medicine.
Referral is a professional skill, not a failure.
All share ethics: confidentiality, consent, do no harm.
title: Counseling vs Clinical vs Psychiatry

points: Listen to understand, not to reply.
Paraphrase in your own shorter words — check: 'Did I get that right?'
Summarize key themes at transitions.
Notice what is NOT said: pauses, topic changes, contradictions.
Avoid interrupting with advice while they talk.
title: Active Listening

points: Name the emotion beneath the client's words.
Formula: 'You feel ___ because ___.'
Reflect deeper feelings — anger often covers hurt.
Reflect positive feelings too: hope, pride, relief.
Keep it tentative — let the client confirm or correct.
title: Reflecting Feelings

points: 1. Build trust — create safety with warmth and empathy.
2. Assess — map the problem together.
3. Set goals — clear, measurable, owned by the client.
4. Intervene — techniques, experiments, homework.
5. Terminate well — review gains, plan for setbacks.
title: Stages of the Counseling Process

points: The partnership predicts success better than any technique.
Bordin's 3 parts: bond, shared goals, agreed tasks.
Empathy — not sympathy — is the heart of it.
Ruptures are normal; a repaired rupture builds deeper trust.
Cultural humility protects the alliance across differences.
title: Therapeutic Alliance

points: Thoughts, feelings and behaviors form a loop — shift one corner.
Thought records: write evidence for and against the thought.
Name thinking traps: catastrophizing, mind reading, 'shoulds'.
Exposure: face fears step by step, easiest first.
Behavioral activation: action first — mood follows.
title: CBT Techniques

points: Created by Marsha Linehan for intense emotions.
Mindfulness: observe the present without judgment.
TIPP for crisis: cold water, exercise, paced breathing.
DEAR MAN: ask for what you need, clearly.
GIVE keeps relationships; FAST keeps self-respect.
title: DBT Skills

points: Fighting painful thoughts IS the problem — drop the rope.
Defusion: thoughts are words, not facts.
Acceptance: make room for feelings instead of battling them.
You are the sky; thoughts and feelings are the weather.
Values guide daily choices; take committed action anyway.
title: ACT: Acceptance & Commitment

points: Focus on solutions and strengths, not problem history.
Miracle question: what would be different tomorrow morning?
Exceptions prove you already have working strategies.
Scaling 1–10 turns vague feelings into trackable progress.
Coping questions honor your resilience: 'How did you keep going?'
title: Solution-Focused Brief Therapy

points: Rogers: you have a natural drive toward growth.
Unconditional positive regard — accepted, never judged.
Empathic understanding of your inner world.
Congruence: the therapist is genuine, not masked.
The client leads; advice is minimized.
title: Person-Centered Counseling

points: Focus on the here and now — awareness itself heals.
Empty chair: speak to the imagined person, then answer as them.
Exaggerate a gesture until the hidden feeling surfaces.
'Top dog vs underdog': notice your inner critic battle.
Own your words: say 'I won't' instead of 'I can't'.
title: Gestalt Therapy

points: Gottman's Four Horsemen: criticism, contempt, defensiveness, stonewalling.
Complain about behavior — never attack character.
5:1 ratio: five positive moments for every negative one.
Repair attempts: humor, touch, 'I need a break'.
69% of problems are perpetual — learn to dialogue, not solve.
title: Couples Counseling

points: 6–10 members heal through each other.
Yalom's universality: 'I am not alone in this.'
Altruism: helping others heals you too.
Stages: forming, storming, norming, performing.
Confidentiality and screening keep the group safe.
title: Group Counseling

points: Children process big feelings through play, not talk.
Child-centered: the therapist follows the child's lead.
Sand tray: build inner worlds in miniature.
Filial therapy trains parents to play at home.
Evidence-based for ages 3–12: anxiety, trauma, grief.
title: Play Therapy

points: Stabilize first — don't dig into history.
ABC: build rapport, boil down the problem, cope.
Ask about suicide directly — it does NOT plant the idea.
Safety plan: warning signs, coping steps, trusted contacts.
Counselor self-care: you can't pour from an empty cup.
title: Crisis Intervention

points: Grief has no timeline — stages are not a ladder.
Worden's tasks: accept reality, feel the pain, adjust, keep connection.
Presence beats platitudes: 'I'm here.'
Don't rush, compare losses, or offer empty reasons.
Continuing bonds: letters, rituals, meaning-making.
title: Grief Counseling

points: Ask 'What happened to you?' — not 'What's wrong with you?'
Safety first: a calm, predictable space.
Trust: keep promises, explain every decision.
Give the client choice and control over pacing.
Never force trauma details — stabilize first.
title: Trauma-Informed Counseling

points: Addiction hijacks the brain's reward system.
Stages of change: precontemplation to maintenance.
Motivational interviewing draws out THEIR reasons to change.
HALT: Hungry, Angry, Lonely, Tired — classic trigger warnings.
Relapse prevention: map high-risk situations, plan coping.
title: Addiction Counseling

points: Autonomy: the client's right to choose comes first.
Beneficence: do good. Nonmaleficence: do no harm.
Justice: fair, equal treatment for every client.
Fidelity: keep promises, stay honest and loyal.
Avoid dual relationships — never be friend AND counselor.
title: Counseling Ethics

points: Confidentiality is the foundation of therapy.
Limits are explained clearly at the very first session.
Imminent danger to self → the counselor must act.
Tarasoff duty: warn an identifiable person who is threatened.
Child or elder abuse must be reported to authorities.
title: Confidentiality & Its Limits
